parsed.explanation: The parent regime imposes real traveler-facing exposures: passport/visa sex-marker restrictions, a cable directing officers to refuse applications where sex is doubted, potential lifetime fraud findings, documented custody and immigration-detention abuse, and foreign governments' travel advisories after detained visitors. Those are universal or high-frequency exposures with partial (though genuinely functioning and partially successful) judicial remedies — placing the parent around 0.55. This division adds nothing visitor-facing beyond the parent: its facility ban covers public-school students only, with no adult bathroom rule, no criminal exposure for adult facility use, no police targeting documented, a dead-letter sodomy statute, and employment protections plus municipal non-discrimination ordinances as climate signals. Uncertainty (custody placement, religious-exemption application to trans service refusals) is open-question weight, not exposure. Document/border friction remains the operative exposure, so the division sits modestly above the parent average, in the lower Reduced Risk band.
